c.tagline: Cowboy heart of the Rockies - Stampede spirit and the gateway to Banff.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares start around C$3.80 plus per-km and per-minute charges. App-based Uber and Lyft both operate citywide and are often cheaper.

emergency.note: 911 is the single emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance across Canada; 811 (Health Link) is Alberta's non-emergency health line.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: The east end of downtown around the drop-in centre and some CTrain platforms can feel uncomfortable late at night.

hood_desc: Calgary's high-rise core plus the buzzing Beltline just to the south, home to the Calgary Tower, Stephen Avenue's shops and restaurants, and the +15 indoor skywalk network; best for first-timers who want to be central and walkable.
A trendy, village-like district just across the Bow River with independent boutiques, cafes, craft-beer bars and cinemas; suits travelers who want a compact, hip neighborhood feel.

Calgary's oldest neighborhood and one of its coolest - antique shops, art galleries, live-music venues, breweries and farm-to-table restaurants along 9th Avenue SE; great for creative, indie-minded visitors.
The 'Red Mile' entertainment strip packed with bars, patios, restaurants and boutiques, spilling into leafy Mission along 4th Street SW; the go-to area for nightlife and dining.
A quieter, historic riverside neighborhood northeast of downtown with a strong local food scene, Italian roots and easy CTrain access; good for a relaxed, residential base close to the action.

water.note: Tap water is safe and high quality throughout the city.

transit.pay: Tap a contactless credit/debit card or phone, or use the My Fare mobile app or a physical Connect card, at CTrain platform machines and on buses. One adult fare is about C$3.70 and covers 90 minutes of transfers. The downtown stretch of 7th Avenue S is a free-fare zone - CTrain rides between City Hall and Downtown West/Kerby stations cost nothing.
transit.hours: CTrain runs roughly 4:30am-1am (later on weekends); frequent MAX BRT and bus routes cover the rest, with reduced late-night service.

train: Rocky Mountaineer (seasonal tourist rail to Banff and Vancouver)
bus: Red Arrow / Ebus / FlixBus (intercity to Edmonton, Banff, Red Deer)

transit.m: Route 300 BRT (Airport/City Centre) to downtown (~45 min)
Route 100 bus to McKnight-Westwinds CTrain then Blue Line downtown (~50 min)
